Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $|0\rangle\in H$ be a specified unit input vector, let $A:H\to H$ be a supplied measurement-free unitary, and let $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$. The access contract supplies and charges calls to $A$, its inverse $A^\dagger$, the good phase reflection
$
S_{\mathrm{good}}:=I_H-2\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},
$
and the zero-input phase reflection
$
S_0:=I_H-2|0\rangle\langle0|.
$
The signs are part of the contract: $S_{\mathrm{good}}$ is $-I$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ and $+I$ on its orthogonal complement. Reflection about the prepared state is the composite $A S_0 A^\dagger$, with its component calls charged unless a separate direct-reflection access is supplied.

Put $|\psi\rangle=A|0\rangle$ and define the initial success weight
$
a:=\|\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle\|^2\in[0,1].
$
When $a>0$, define $|G\rangle:=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle/\sqrt a$. When $a<1$, define $|B\rangle:=(I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})|\psi\rangle/\sqrt{1-a}$. These vectors are normalized and lie respectively in the range and kernel of $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$. If $a=0$ or $a=1$, the corresponding zero component is omitted and no vector is normalized from it. With this convention,
$
|\psi\rangle=\sqrt a\,|G\rangle+\sqrt{1-a}\,|B\rangle
$
means the sum of the nonzero component terms. Under the projective measurement $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$, the probability of the good outcome is $a$; the finite-dimensional rank-one density and projective-measurement outcome laws are [[thm-qc-unit-vector-projector-is-density]] and [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

The output task may return the conditional quantum state after the good outcome; that state is defined only on a positive-probability branch and is supported in $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ by [[thm-qc-projective-conditional-state]]. A classical output additionally requires $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ to be diagonal in a specified output basis and a costed coherent or ordinary verifier. An arbitrary projection does not supply a classical predicate.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$. Fix the two signs

$$R_\Pi:=2\Pi-I,\qquad S_\Pi:=I-2\Pi=-R_\Pi.$$

Thus $R_\Pi$ acts as $+I$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ and $-I$ on $\ker\Pi$; $S_\Pi$ reverses those signs. They are not interchangeable inside a controlled block. For a unit vector $\psi$, the rank-one reflection is $R_\psi=2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|-I$ with the Dirac convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]].

An access model counts a direct reflection as one primitive call only when that call is explicitly declared. Controlled reflection access is a separate declaration. If $|0\rangle$ is a specified unit input in the same space $H$, the state is prepared as $\psi=U|0\rangle$ for a declared unitary $U$, and a reflection is implemented by conjugating $R_0=2|0\rangle\langle0|-I$, the construction is $UR_0U^\dagger$ and its cost must include the calls to $U$, $R_0$, and $U^\dagger$. A state vector or matrix description alone implies neither an efficient reflection nor inverse access.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection. The operators $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$ and $S_\Pi=I-2\Pi$ are self-adjoint unitary involutions, with $R_\Pi=-S_\Pi$. On $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ they act as $+I$ and $-I$, respectively; on $\ker\Pi$ they act as $-I$ and $+I$. In control-first order,

$$C(S_\Pi)=(Z_C)C(R_\Pi),\qquad Z_C:=\operatorname{diag}(I_H,-I_H)=Z\otimes I_H.$$

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\sin(z+w)=\sin z\cos w+\cos z\sin w,$$
$$\cos(z+w)=\cos z\cos w-\sin z\sin w,$$
$$\sinh(z+w)=\sinh z\cosh w+\cosh z\sinh w,$$
$$\cosh(z+w)=\cosh z\cosh w+\sinh z\sinh w.$$

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(x+\pi/2)=\cos x,\quad\cos(x+\pi/2)=-\sin x,\quad\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x,\quad\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x.$$
In particular,
$$\sin(\pi/2)=1,\quad\cos(\pi/2)=0,\quad\sin\pi=0,\quad\cos\pi=-1.$$

Let $\gamma$ be the unique smallest positive zero of cosine supplied by [[thm-cosine-has-a-smallest-positive-zero]]. Define
$$\pi:=2\gamma.$$

Thus $\pi>0$ and $\pi/2=\gamma$.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

derivations.claim: Put $c=\sqrt{1-a}=\cos\theta$ and $s=\sqrt a=\sin\theta$. The two components $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle$ and $(I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})|\psi\rangle$ are orthogonal because $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ is an orthogonal projection. Their nonzero normalized vectors therefore form an orthonormal pair, and $|\psi\rangle=c|B\rangle+s|G\rangle$. The angle $\theta$ is unique in $(0,\pi/2)$: sine is continuous there, has endpoint values $0,1$, and is strictly increasing because its derivative is the positive cosine before the first positive cosine zero.

In the ordered basis $(|B\rangle,|G\rangle)$, $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, so $S_{\mathrm{good}}=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Also $A S_0 A^\dagger=I-2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$, since $A|0\rangle=|\psi\rangle$. The matrix of this latter reflection is [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]
$
\begin{pmatrix}1-2c^2&-2cs\\-2cs&1-2s^2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}-\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\-\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix}.
$
The product $Q=- (A S_0 A^\dagger)S_{\mathrm{good}}$ is therefore the displayed rotation matrix. This proves invariance and the claimed restriction.

If $a=0$, then $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle=0$, so $S_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle$, while $A S_0 A^\dagger|\psi\rangle=-|\psi\rangle$; hence $Q|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle$. If $a=1$, then $S_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle=-|\psi\rangle$ and $A S_0 A^\dagger|\psi\rangle=-|\psi\rangle$, hence $Q|\psi\rangle=-|\psi\rangle$. No zero component is normalized.

derivations.claim: Assume $0<a<1$. The initial coordinates in the invariant ordered basis are $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Multiplication by the matrix in [F1] and the addition formulas in [F4] send $(\cos t,\sin t)$ to $(\cos(t+2\theta),\sin(t+2\theta))$. Starting at $t=\theta$, induction on $k$ therefore gives coordinates $(\cos((2k+1)\theta),\sin((2k+1)\theta))$ after $k$ iterates.

The good component is the second coordinate, so its squared norm is $\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)$. The prepared unit vector gives a density operator by [F2], and [F3] identifies this squared component norm with the projective-measurement outcome probability.

If $a=0$, then $\theta=0$ and [F1] gives success probability $0=\sin^2((2k+1)0)$. If $a=1$, then $\theta=\pi/2$; [F1] changes only the global sign on each iterate, and [F5] gives $\sin^2((2k+1)\pi/2)=1$. Thus the same formula holds at both endpoints.

Input a coherent sampler $A$, an orthogonal success projection $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$, and a fixed integer $k\ge0$, under the access contract of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]]. Additionally supply the good/bad projective instrument $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$, charging each measurement and its implementation costs separately. Prepare $|\psi\rangle=A|0\rangle$. In the displayed right-to-left operator convention, set
$
Q:=-A(I-2|0\rangle\langle0|)A^\dagger(I-2\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}).
$
Apply $Q$ exactly $k$ times. Then apply the projective instrument $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$. On a positive-probability good outcome return its conditional quantum state; on the bad outcome return fail. The conditional state exists only on a positive-probability branch, as in [[thm-qc-projective-conditional-state]].

For the classical-output specialization, additionally require $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ to be diagonal in the designated output basis and supply a costed verifier. Measure that basis only after the success-projector instrument has accepted; verify the resulting candidate and return it or fail. No arbitrary-projector-to-classical-predicate conversion is implicit.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

Input a coherent sampler with an exactly represented known success weight $a\in[0,1]$. For the finite rational-input procedure, $a$ is given as a binary rational; exact algebraic inputs are also allowed when the supplied representation supports exact comparisons. If $a=0$, return fail without normalizing a good component. If $a=1$, prepare $A|0\rangle$, apply the declared good/bad projective instrument, and return its good conditional state (or, in the diagonal classical-output specialization, measure and verify the output).

For $0<a<1$, set $\theta:=\arcsin\sqrt a\in(0,\pi/2)$, using the principal inverse-sine and nonnegative-square-root conventions of [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]]. Then $\theta$ is the unique angle with $\sin^2\theta=a$. Set $K:=\lceil1/\sqrt a\rceil$, equivalently the least positive integer $K$ with $K^2a\ge1$. For each integer $k=0,\ldots,K$, compute $p_k=\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)$ exactly by the rational recurrence
$
x_0=1,\qquad x_1=1-2a,\qquad x_{n+1}=2(1-2a)x_n-x_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad p_k=(1-x_{2k+1})/2.
$
Indeed, writing $x_n=\cos(2n\theta)$, double-angle gives $x_0=1$, $x_1=\cos(2\theta)=1-2a$, and cosine addition gives the displayed recurrence. Also $\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)=(1-\cos((4k+2)\theta))/2=(1-x_{2k+1})/2$. Choose the least $k$ attaining the maximum of this finite list. Run the fixed-$k$ procedure [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]], verify when a classical candidate is requested, and return the good conditional output or fail. For rational $a$, every $x_n$ and $p_k$ is rational, so the comparisons are exact. No time bound for this classical preprocessing is claimed.

$
The endpoints $a=0$ and $a=1$ are included by direct evaluation, without normalizing a zero component.

$$\sin(x+\pi/2)=\cos x,\quad \cos(x+\pi/2)=-\sin x,\quad \sin(-x)=-\sin x,\quad \cos(-x)=\cos x.$$
On the common natural domains of the two sides,
$$\tan(\pi/2-x)=\cot x,\quad \cot(\pi/2-x)=\tan x,\quad \sec(\pi/2-x)=\csc x,\quad \csc(\pi/2-x)=\sec x,$$

$$\tan(\pi-x)=-\tan x,\quad \cot(\pi-x)=-\cot x,\quad \sec(\pi-x)=-\sec x,\quad \csc(\pi-x)=\csc x.$$
The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]], [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]], [[def-tangent-cotangent-secant-cosecant]].

Input a coherent sampler with an exactly represented known success weight $a\in[0,1]$. For the finite rational-input procedure, $a$ is given as a binary rational; exact algebraic inputs are also allowed when the supplied representation supports exact comparisons. If $a=0$, return fail without normalizing a good component. If $a=1$, prepare $A|0\rangle$, apply the declared good/bad projective instrument, and return its good conditional state (or, in the diagonal classical-output specialization, measure and verify the output).

For $0<a<1$, set $\theta:=\arcsin\sqrt a\in(0,\pi/2)$, using the principal inverse-sine and nonnegative-square-root conventions of [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]]. Then $\theta$ is the unique angle with $\sin^2\theta=a$. Set $K:=\lceil1/\sqrt a\rceil$, equivalently the least positive integer $K$ with $K^2a\ge1$. For each integer $k=0,\ldots,K$, compute $p_k=\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)$ exactly by the rational recurrence
$
x_0=1,\qquad x_1=1-2a,\qquad x_{n+1}=2(1-2a)x_n-x_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad p_k=(1-x_{2k+1})/2.
$
Indeed, writing $x_n=\cos(2n\theta)$, double-angle gives $x_0=1$, $x_1=\cos(2\theta)=1-2a$, and cosine addition gives the displayed recurrence. Also $\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)=(1-\cos((4k+2)\theta))/2=(1-x_{2k+1})/2$. Choose the least $k$ attaining the maximum of this finite list. Run the fixed-$k$ procedure [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]], verify when a classical candidate is requested, and return the good conditional output or fail. For rational $a$, every $x_n$ and $p_k$ is rational, so the comparisons are exact. No time bound for this classical preprocessing is claimed.

For a fixed $k$-iterate procedure, the displayed factorization of $Q$ uses $k+1$ forward calls to $A$, $k$ inverse calls to $A^\dagger$, $k$ good-subspace phase operations, and $k$ zero-input phase operations. It then uses one projective good/bad instrument. If classical output verification is requested, count its supplied verifier separately (one call when the task model assigns one query to verification). Controlled $A$, state-preparation synthesis, gates, and classical costs are separate access coordinates and are not inferred to be free.

For $0<a<1$, let $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$ satisfy $\sin^2\theta=a$, and let $k$ be the maximizer selected by [[alg-qa-12-known-amplitude-amplification]]. Its success probability is at least $\max\{a,1-a\}$. The $a=0$ branch returns fail, and the $a=1$ branch succeeds with probability $1$.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

Input a prepared sampler $A$, its inverse $A^\dagger$, an orthogonal good projection $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$, and an exactly represented known $a\in[0,1]$ equal to the success weight. The model must supply the coherent flag unitary
$
C_{\mathrm{good}}=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\otimes X+(I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})\otimes I
$
and its inverse, a clean flag qubit $F$, a clean temporary qubit $T$, external clean implementation workspace, and exact real arithmetic and controlled flag-rotation access, including inverse rotations. These are explicit capabilities; a bare phase reflection does not supply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$, and no finite-bit gate synthesis is asserted. The input data space is the possibly abstract space $H$ and specified vector $|0\rangle$ of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]]; no full classical description or computational-basis test for that vector is inferred. No controlled access to $A$ is required.

If $a=0$, return fail without normalizing a good component. If $a=1$, prepare $A|0\rangle$ and apply $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$. Supply and charge that instrument directly, or construct it by applying $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to data and a clean scratch bit, measuring only that bit, and applying $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$; this costs two flag calls and one bit measurement and resets the scratch. Return the good conditional state; in the diagonal classical-output case, measure the designated output and verify it.

For $0<a<1$, set $\theta:=\arcsin\sqrt a\in(0,\pi/2)$, using [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]], and define
$
m=\left\lceil\frac{\pi}{4\theta}-\frac12\right\rceil,\qquad
\theta'=\frac{\pi}{4m+2},\qquad r=\frac{\sin^2\theta'}{a}.
$
Since $m\ge\pi/(4\theta)-1/2$, we have $4m+2\ge\pi/\theta$, hence $0<\theta'\le\theta<\pi/2$. Sine is strictly increasing on $[0,\pi/2]$, so $0<\sin^2\theta'\le\sin^2\theta=a$, proving $0<r\le1$; the square roots in the following rotation are the unique nonnegative roots. On the enlarged data, flag, and temporary registers, construct $A'$ by the following finite gate sequence:

1. Start every added register in $|0\rangle$ and apply $A$ to the data.
2. Apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to the data and temporary bit.
3. Controlled on the temporary bit being $1$, apply the flag rotation
$
R_r=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt{1-r}&-\sqrt r\\ \sqrt r&\sqrt{1-r}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad R_r|0\rangle=\sqrt{1-r}|0\rangle+\sqrt r|1\rangle .
$
4. Apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$ to uncompute the temporary bit. This full unitary is $A'$; its inverse reverses these operations and uses $A^\dagger$.

The logical enlarged space is $H'=H\otimes F\otimes T$, with specified input $|0'\rangle=|0\rangle_H|0\rangle_F|0\rangle_T$ and success projector $\Pi'=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_F\otimes I_T$. This uses one controlled-$S_0$ call, two Toffolis and four $X$ gates per enlarged zero reflection. Controlled $S_0$ is an additional capability and is not inferred from ordinary $S_0$ access.
- **Good reflection.** In the constructed mode, apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to $(H,q)$ with external scratch $q=0$, then $CZ(q,F)$, then $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$ to $(H,q)$. This uses two flag calls and one $CZ$ per $S'_{\mathrm{good}}$. An alternative direct mode explicitly supplies and charges $S'_{\mathrm{good}}$ instead. Here $X$, Toffoli and $CZ$ are the exact supplied qubit gates of [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], [[def-qc-toffoli-and-fredkin]] and [[def-qc-controlled-z-and-swap]], with their gate costs charged.

The scratch $q$ starts and ends in $0$ for each reflection and may be reused. It is external implementation workspace, not part of the logical input $|0'\rangle$ or the projector defining $S'_0$. The constructions implement the displayed logical operators on every vector of $H'$ with clean scratch; neither assumes $T=0$ to implement $I_T$ in the good projector.

Multiplying by $4\theta>0$ gives $4m\theta+2\theta\ge\pi$, hence $4m+2\ge\pi/\theta$ and $0<\theta'=\pi/(4m+2)\le\theta<\pi/2$. By sine monotonicity in [F6], $0<\sin^2\theta'\le\sin^2\theta=a$, so $0<r=\sin^2\theta'/a\le1$ and the two nonnegative square roots used in the supplied flag rotation are defined.

In the constructed zero reflection, on fixed logical flag/temporary bits $f,t$, the four $X$ gates and two Toffolis compute and then erase $q=(1-f)(1-t)$. The data sees $S_0$ exactly when $f=t=0$, and identity otherwise. This is $I-2|0\rangle\langle0|_H\otimes|00\rangle\langle00|_{F,T}=S'_0$. In the constructed good reflection, split any data vector as $v_g+v_b$ with $v_g=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}v$. The first flag call records $1$ on $v_g$ and $0$ on $v_b$ in $q$; $CZ(q,F)$ multiplies only $v_g$ with $F=1$ by $-1$, and the inverse flag call clears $q$. Thus it is $I-2\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_F\otimes I_T=S'_{\mathrm{good}}$ for arbitrary $T$. Linearity extends both calculations to every logical vector with clean external scratch. Direct modes supply these same operators by hypothesis.

For the optional constructed terminal instrument, the coherent computation into $d$ records exactly the predicate defining $\Pi'$. Measuring only $d$ therefore leaves the unnormalized logical branches $\Pi'\rho\Pi'$ and $(I-\Pi')\rho(I-\Pi')$; reversing the conjunction and flag computation clears $d,q$ within either branch without measuring the good component separately. This is the stated projective instrument. The direct mode supplies it by hypothesis.

In the prepared state, the good and bad components are $\sqrt a\,|G\rangle$ and $\sqrt{1-a}\,|B\rangle$. The coherent flag operation sets the temporary bit exactly on the good component; the controlled rotation places flag-$1$ amplitude $\sqrt r$ on that component and leaves the bad component with flag $0$; uncomputing the temporary bit returns it to $0$. Thus $A'|0'\rangle$ has good component $\sqrt{ar}\,|G\rangle|1\rangle|0\rangle$. Since $ar=\sin^2\theta'$, the modified pair $(A',\Pi')$ has success weight $\sin^2\theta'$.

By step 1.2 the selected access modes implement the exact modified-pair iterates with external scratch reset after each call. The two-dimensional amplification plane is spanned by the good and bad components of $A'|0'\rangle$, both with $T=0$ by step 2.1; it therefore retains $T=0$. The rotation theorem [F2] applied after $m$ iterates gives the following good probability. Input a prepared sampler $A$, its inverse $A^\dagger$, an orthogonal good projection $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$, and an exactly represented known $a\in[0,1]$ equal to the success weight. The model must supply the coherent flag unitary
$
C_{\mathrm{good}}=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\otimes X+(I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})\otimes I
$
and its inverse, a clean flag qubit $F$, a clean temporary qubit $T$, external clean implementation workspace, and exact real arithmetic and controlled flag-rotation access, including inverse rotations. These are explicit capabilities; a bare phase reflection does not supply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$, and no finite-bit gate synthesis is asserted. The input data space is the possibly abstract space $H$ and specified vector $|0\rangle$ of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]]; no full classical description or computational-basis test for that vector is inferred. No controlled access to $A$ is required.

If $a=0$, return fail without normalizing a good component. If $a=1$, prepare $A|0\rangle$ and apply $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$. Supply and charge that instrument directly, or construct it by applying $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to data and a clean scratch bit, measuring only that bit, and applying $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$; this costs two flag calls and one bit measurement and resets the scratch. Return the good conditional state; in the diagonal classical-output case, measure the designated output and verify it.

For $0<a<1$, set $\theta:=\arcsin\sqrt a\in(0,\pi/2)$, using [[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]], and define
$
m=\left\lceil\frac{\pi}{4\theta}-\frac12\right\rceil,\qquad
\theta'=\frac{\pi}{4m+2},\qquad r=\frac{\sin^2\theta'}{a}.
$
Since $m\ge\pi/(4\theta)-1/2$, we have $4m+2\ge\pi/\theta$, hence $0<\theta'\le\theta<\pi/2$. Sine is strictly increasing on $[0,\pi/2]$, so $0<\sin^2\theta'\le\sin^2\theta=a$, proving $0<r\le1$; the square roots in the following rotation are the unique nonnegative roots. On the enlarged data, flag, and temporary registers, construct $A'$ by the following finite gate sequence:

1. Start every added register in $|0\rangle$ and apply $A$ to the data.
2. Apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to the data and temporary bit.
3. Controlled on the temporary bit being $1$, apply the flag rotation
$
R_r=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt{1-r}&-\sqrt r\\ \sqrt r&\sqrt{1-r}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad R_r|0\rangle=\sqrt{1-r}|0\rangle+\sqrt r|1\rangle .
$
4. Apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$ to uncompute the temporary bit. This full unitary is $A'$; its inverse reverses these operations and uses $A^\dagger$.

The logical enlarged space is $H'=H\otimes F\otimes T$, with specified input $|0'\rangle=|0\rangle_H|0\rangle_F|0\rangle_T$ and success projector $\Pi'=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_F\otimes I_T$. Its required reflections are $S'_0=I_{H'}-2|0'\rangle\langle0'|$ and $S'_{\mathrm{good}}=I_{H'}-2\Pi'$. Select and charge the following access modes before execution.

- **Zero reflection.** Either explicitly supply one direct $S'_0$ call, or supply controlled access $C(S_0)$ to the original data reflection $S_0=I_H-2|0\rangle\langle0|$. In the latter mode, initialize an external scratch qubit $q$ to $0$; apply $X$ to $F,T$, Toffoli$(F,T;q)$, $C(S_0)$ controlled by $q$ on $H$, Toffoli$(F,T;q)$, and $X$ to $F,T$ again. This uses one controlled-$S_0$ call, two Toffolis and four $X$ gates per enlarged zero reflection. Controlled $S_0$ is an additional capability and is not inferred from ordinary $S_0$ access.
- **Good reflection.** In the constructed mode, apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ to $(H,q)$ with external scratch $q=0$, then $CZ(q,F)$, then $C_{\mathrm{good}}^\dagger$ to $(H,q)$. This uses two flag calls and one $CZ$ per $S'_{\mathrm{good}}$. An alternative direct mode explicitly supplies and charges $S'_{\mathrm{good}}$ instead. Here $X$, Toffoli and $CZ$ are the exact supplied qubit gates of [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], [[def-qc-toffoli-and-fredkin]] and [[def-qc-controlled-z-and-swap]], with their gate costs charged.

The scratch $q$ starts and ends in $0$ for each reflection and may be reused. It is external implementation workspace, not part of the logical input $|0'\rangle$ or the projector defining $S'_0$. The constructions implement the displayed logical operators on every vector of $H'$ with clean scratch; neither assumes $T=0$ to implement $I_T$ in the good projector.

Prepare $A'|0'\rangle$, apply exactly $m$ iterates $-A'S'_0A'^\dagger S'_{\mathrm{good}}$, then perform the projective instrument $\{\Pi',I-\Pi'\}$. The terminal instrument is an explicitly supplied, separately charged capability. Alternatively construct it with two external clean bits $q,d$: apply $C_{\mathrm{good}}$ on $(H,q)$, Toffoli$(q,F;d)$, measure only $d$ in the computational basis to obtain the good/bad record, then reverse the Toffoli and the flag call. Both scratch bits return to $0$ on either observed branch; this option adds two flag calls, two Toffolis and one bit measurement, separately from the reflection counts. Return the good conditional output, discarding $F,T$; $T$ is clean and $F=1$ on success. In the diagonal classical-output specialization, measure the designated output after the good outcome and use the supplied verifier.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

For a finite-dimensional unitary $U$, **inverse access** is the explicitly granted operation $U^\dagger=U^{-1}$. Its availability and query or gate charge are recorded separately from forward access, including any controlled access in [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. For a chronological sequence of length $k\ge0$ that applies $U_1$ first and $U_k$ last, the total operator is $W=U_k\cdots U_1$ when $k>0$ and $W=I_H$ when $k=0$. For $k>0$, the inverse sequence applies $U_k^\dagger$ first, then $U_{k-1}^\dagger$, down to $U_1^\dagger$; for $k=0$ it is the empty sequence.

Let $D$ be a finite ordered quantum register and let $A$ be an ordered register of $k\ge0$ ancilla qubits, with Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_D$ and $\mathcal H_A$. Write $|0_A\rangle=|0^k\rangle$, including $|0_A\rangle=1$ when $k=0$. Let $U$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and let $V$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D$.

The register $A$ is a **clean ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when
$$
U(|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle
$$
for every vector $|\psi\rangle_D$. Thus the data operation is independent of the input vector and all clean wires return exactly to zero.

The register $A$ is a **dirty ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when the operator identity $U=V\otimes I_A$ holds on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$. Equivalently, every product input $|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$ is mapped to $V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$, with the same $V$ for every data and ancilla vector. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

For all real $u,v$,

$$|\sin u-\sin v|\le|u-v|,$$

and

$$|\cos u-\cos v|\le|u-v|.$$

Thus sine and cosine are Lipschitz functions on $\mathbb R$, each with
Lipschitz constant $1$.

derivations.claim: In the nontrivial branch $0<a<1$, $m\le\pi/(4\theta)+1/2$. Since $\sqrt a=\sin\theta\le\theta$ by [F5] and $a\le1$, $m\le(\pi/4+1/2)/\sqrt a$. The direct $a=1$ branch uses a constant number of calls.

The initial $A'$ contributes one forward $A$, two flag calls and one controlled flag rotation. Each of the $m$ iterates contains one $A'$ and one $A'^\dagger$, contributing one forward and one inverse $A$, four flag calls and two controlled rotations. Thus these parts contribute $m+1$ forward $A$, $m$ inverse $A^\dagger$, $4m+2$ flag calls and $2m+1$ rotations. Each constructed good reflection contributes two further flag calls and one $CZ$, giving $6m+2$ flag calls and $m$ $CZ$ gates. Direct good-reflection access instead contributes $m$ calls of its own coordinate and leaves the flag total $4m+2$.

Each constructed zero reflection uses one controlled-$S_0$, two Toffolis and four $X$ gates; $m$ repetitions give $m,2m,4m$, respectively. Direct zero-reflection access instead uses $m$ direct $S'_0$ calls. The same external clean scratch is reused, since the exact reflection constructions return it to zero. The optional terminal construction uses two flag calls and two Toffolis around one bit measurement, with a second external bit, so its addition gives the stated $6m+4$ or $4m+4$ flag total. No other step invokes $C_{\mathrm{good}}$; the separately supplied terminal mode has no constituent flag count inferred.

The bounds in steps 1.1–1.3 are $O(a^{-1/2})$. By [F2]–[F4], they count only the declared query and access coordinates; exact arithmetic, synthesis, preparation, measurement, and any final verifier retain their separate costs. The success guarantee is [F1] together with [[thm-qa-12-exact-success-guarantee]].

This is a sequential randomized procedure, not a bounded-$T$ circuit family. Fix $c=3/2$. For rounds $\ell=1,2,\ldots$, compute the finite integer $M_\ell=\lceil c^\ell\rceil$ by exact rational arithmetic. In classical-output mode, require the diagonal-predicate specialization of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]] and a costed verifier that accepts exactly the basis labels designated good by $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$; measure the designated output basis only after the good/bad instrument and then run the verifier.

1. On a fresh register prepare $A|0\rangle$ and perform the declared good/bad projective instrument. On a bad outcome, continue to step 2. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted.

2. Prepare $A|0\rangle$ on a second fresh register. Draw $j$ uniformly from the finite set $\{1,\ldots,M_\ell\}$, apply exactly $j$ standard $Q$-iterates, and perform the good/bad instrument. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted. If the outcome is bad or verification rejects, discard the registers and continue to round $\ell+1$.

The random choice is fresh and independent in each round; the schedule depends only on $\ell$, never on the unknown $a$. Every round is finite. When $a=0$, the loop runs forever and does not decide whether the good set is empty.

Let $a\in[0,1]$ be the initial success weight and let $\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$ be the unique angle satisfying $\sin^2\theta=a$. After exactly $k\ge0$ standard amplitude-amplification iterates, the probability of the good outcome of $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$ is
$
\sin^2((2k+1)\theta).
$
The endpoints $a=0$ and $a=1$ are included by direct evaluation, without normalizing a zero component.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator and $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ a finite projective measurement on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Put $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$. If $p_a>0$, then

$$\rho_a:=\frac{P_a\rho P_a}{p_a}$$

is a density operator whose image $\operatorname{im}(\rho_a):=\{\rho_a x:x\in H\}$ is contained in $\operatorname{im}(P_a)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). This statement assigns a conditional state only on positive-probability branches.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\sin(z+w)=\sin z\cos w+\cos z\sin w,$$
$$\cos(z+w)=\cos z\cos w-\sin z\sin w,$$
$$\sinh(z+w)=\sinh z\cosh w+\cosh z\sinh w,$$
$$\cosh(z+w)=\cosh z\cosh w+\sinh z\sinh w.$$

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]], [[lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[lem-binomial-theorem-over-complex-numbers]], [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]].

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

Assume $0<a<1$, and let $0<\theta<\pi/2$ satisfy $\sin^2\theta=a$. The identity $\sin^2x=(1-\cos(2x))/2$ gives
$
p_M=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\sin^2((2j+1)\theta)
=\frac12-\frac1{2M}\sum_{j=1}^M\cos((4j+2)\theta).
$
The cosine sum is the real part of $e^{i6\theta}\sum_{r=0}^{M-1}e^{i4r\theta}$. By [F6], this finite geometric sum has modulus
$
\frac{|1-e^{i4M\theta}|}{|1-e^{i4\theta}|}
=\frac{|\sin(2M\theta)|}{|\sin(2\theta)|}
\le\frac1{|\sin(2\theta)|}.
$
Taking real parts therefore gives
$
p_M\ge\frac12-\frac1{2M|\sin(2\theta)|}.
$

If $0<a<3/4$, then $\sin(2\theta)=2\sqrt{a(1-a)}\ge\sqrt a$. Since $M_\ell\to\infty$, some finite round has $M_\ell\ge2/\sqrt a$, after which [F1]–[F2] give a conditional per-round success probability at least $p_{M_\ell}\ge1/4$. If $a\ge3/4$, the direct sample in each round succeeds with probability at least $3/4$. Thus in either case there is a finite round after which every fresh round has conditional success probability bounded below by a fixed positive constant.

Registers and randomness are fresh each round, so after $r$ rounds beyond the finite threshold in step 2.1, the probability of still not returning is at most $(3/4)^r$ in the first case and $(1/4)^r$ in the second. Both tend to zero. Since every output is returned only after the good instrument outcome (and verification when required), no bad output is returned; on every positive-probability good branch [F4] supplies its conditional state.

If $a=0$, every fresh preparation has zero projection onto $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$, so each good outcome has probability zero by [F3]. The procedure therefore never returns and runs forever, as specified in [F1].

This is a sequential randomized procedure, not a bounded-$T$ circuit family. Fix $c=3/2$. For rounds $\ell=1,2,\ldots$, compute the finite integer $M_\ell=\lceil c^\ell\rceil$ by exact rational arithmetic. In classical-output mode, require the diagonal-predicate specialization of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]] and a costed verifier that accepts exactly the basis labels designated good by $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$; measure the designated output basis only after the good/bad instrument and then run the verifier.

1. On a fresh register prepare $A|0\rangle$ and perform the declared good/bad projective instrument. On a bad outcome, continue to step 2. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted.

2. Prepare $A|0\rangle$ on a second fresh register. Draw $j$ uniformly from the finite set $\{1,\ldots,M_\ell\}$, apply exactly $j$ standard $Q$-iterates, and perform the good/bad instrument. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted. If the outcome is bad or verification rejects, discard the registers and continue to round $\ell+1$.

The random choice is fresh and independent in each round; the schedule depends only on $\ell$, never on the unknown $a$. Every round is finite. When $a=0$, the loop runs forever and does not decide whether the good set is empty.

For $0<a<1$, let $\sin^2\theta=a$. For every integer $M\ge1$, the second fresh sample with $j$ uniform on $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ has good-outcome probability
$
p_M=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\sin^2((2j+1)\theta)
=\frac12-\frac1{2M}\sum_{j=1}^M\cos((4j+2)\theta)
\ge\frac12-\frac1{2M|\sin(2\theta)|}.
$
For every $a>0$, the procedure [[alg-qa-12-unknown-amplitude-search]] returns a good output with probability $1$. If $a=0$, it never returns a good output and does not halt.

Let $a\in[0,1]$ be the initial success weight and let $\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$ be the unique angle satisfying $\sin^2\theta=a$. After exactly $k\ge0$ standard amplitude-amplification iterates, the probability of the good outcome of $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$ is
$
\sin^2((2k+1)\theta).
$
The endpoints $a=0$ and $a=1$ are included by direct evaluation, without normalizing a zero component.

Fix a promised input $z$ and a sequential procedure whose elementary steps are deterministic transitions, finite random transitions, finite-outcome measurements, or a single oracle call. At every live history, the next transition has a specified probability law on a finite outcome set; a query step has one successor and issues one call. A halted history is extended by deterministic idle steps that issue no calls.

For $M\in\mathbb N$, let $\Omega_M$ be the finite set of length-$M$ histories with the recursively assigned transition weights. Let $C_M:\Omega_M\to\{0,\ldots,M\}$ count the oracle calls actually executed in those $M$ steps. Define the **expected query cost** on input $z$ by
$$
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{query}}(z):=\sup_{M\in\mathbb N}\mathbb E[C_M]\in[0,\infty],
$$
where each expectation is taken on the finite probability space of the corresponding prefix. Define the pathwise total query count on an infinite history $\omega$ by $C(\omega):=\sup_M C_M(\omega)$. No probability measure or expectation of $C$ on an infinite history space is presumed by this definition.

If a procedure is organized into rounds of at most $K$ elementary steps for some fixed integer $K\ge1$, each containing at most one query, pad each round with deterministic idle steps to exactly $K$ steps. In this padded procedure, its first $R$ rounds are the prefix of length $KR$. Hence the supremum of its finite-round expected query counts equals the displayed finite-step supremum. In particular, query-indexed rounds are valid when each round contains exactly one query, as in Simon sampling.

For a $T$-query quantum algorithm [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]] at input length $n$, its **worst-case quantum query cost** is the maximum number of designated oracle calls over all promised instances in $P_n$ and all measurement branches. When $P_n$ is empty, define this cost to be $0$. For nonempty $P_n$, a finite circuit and finite branch sets ensure that this maximum exists; a solver whose branch counts are not uniformly bounded has infinite worst-case query cost. An expected-query bound is the separate quantity defined by [[def-qa-expected-query-cost]].

In the pure query model, ordinary gates outside the oracle calls are uncharged by the query coordinate. If a task also reports gate, preparation, measurement, or classical costs, those are separate coordinates. Bounded-error query cost uses the same worst-case maximum; its success threshold is the per-instance condition in [[def-qa-bounded-error-promise-correctness]], not an average over oracle inputs.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\sin(z+w)=\sin z\cos w+\cos z\sin w,$$
$$\cos(z+w)=\cos z\cos w-\sin z\sin w,$$
$$\sinh(z+w)=\sinh z\cosh w+\cosh z\sinh w,$$
$$\cosh(z+w)=\cosh z\cosh w+\sinh z\sinh w.$$

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

For all real $u,v$,

$$|\sin u-\sin v|\le|u-v|,$$

and

$$|\cos u-\cos v|\le|u-v|.$$

Thus sine and cosine are Lipschitz functions on $\mathbb R$, each with
Lipschitz constant $1$.

derivations.claim:
For $0<a<3/4$, write $s=\sin(2\theta)=2\sqrt{a(1-a)}\ge\sqrt a$. Once $M_\ell\ge8/s$, [F2] gives amplification-attempt success at least $7/16$, so the conditional probability of reaching the next round is at most $(1-a)(9/16)\le9/16$. If $M_\ell\ge8$, then
$
M_{\ell+1}\le\frac32M_\ell+1\le\frac{13}{8}M_\ell,
$
and the survival-weighted cost ratio of later rounds is at most $(9/16)(13/8)=117/128<1$.

Let $q=3/2$. For every $\ell\ge1$, $q^\ell\ge\ell$: it holds directly for $\ell=1,2$, and if it holds for $\ell\ge2$, then $q^{\ell+1}\ge(3/2)\ell\ge\ell+1$. Thus $M_\ell\ge\ell$. With $N=\lceil8/s\rceil$, we have $M_N\ge N\ge8/s$, so the first threshold index $L$ is at most $N=O(1/s)$. If $L\ge2$, then $M_{L-1}<8/s$ and $M_L=\lceil q^L\rceil\le qM_{L-1}+1<12/s+1\le13/s$; the same bound holds when $L=1$. Before that threshold the $M_\ell$ grow geometrically, so their sum is $O(1/s)$; the $L$ direct preparations and fixed-cost verifications also cost $O(1/s)$. A round that reaches its amplification attempt makes at most four named calls per iterate, at most one extra preparation call, and at most one verifier call for each of its two samples; including the first direct sample, its total is at most $4M_\ell+4$. After the threshold, [F1], step 1.1, and $M_{\ell+1}\le(13/8)M_\ell$ make the survival-weighted worst-case round costs contract by at most $(9/16)(13/8)=117/128<1$. Since $s\ge\sqrt a$, the total is $O(a^{-1/2})$. If $a\ge3/4$, each direct sample succeeds with probability at least $3/4$, and $M_{\ell+1}\le2M_\ell$ for $M_\ell\ge2$; worst-case round costs grow by at most a factor $2$, so survival-weighted costs contract by at most $1/2$, giving $O(1)=O(a^{-1/2})$. Each bound applies to every finite prefix, and taking the supremum in [F4] proves the upper bound without an infinite-history expectation.

For a lower bound at small $a$, fix $u=1/100$ and let $L$ be the first round with $M_L\ge u/\sqrt a$. For every integer $n\ge1$, induction with [F6] gives $|\sin(n\theta)|\le n\sin\theta$: the base case is equality, and the addition formula bounds the next value by $|\sin(n\theta)|+|\sin\theta|$. Therefore the success probability before round $L$ is at most $a+9aM_\ell^2$, accounting for the direct sample and $a(2M_\ell+1)^2\le9aM_\ell^2$ for the amplified sample. As proved in step 2.1, $M_\ell\ge\ell$; therefore $L\le\lceil u/\sqrt a\rceil$. For sufficiently small $a$, $L\ge2$, $M_{L-1}<u/\sqrt a$, and $M_\ell\le(3/2)^\ell+1$; geometric summation gives [given, F1, F3, F6, step 2.1, algebra]
$
\sum_{\ell<L}M_\ell^2
\le \frac{(3/2)^2}{(3/2)^2-1}\frac{u^2}{a}
+\frac{2(3/2)}{(3/2)-1}\frac{u}{\sqrt a}+L
=\frac{1.8u^2}{a}+\frac{6u}{\sqrt a}+L.
$
Hence the chance of any earlier success is at most $16.2u^2+54u\sqrt a+10aL\le16.2u^2+64u\sqrt a+10a$, which tends to $16.2u^2<1/4$. For all sufficiently small $a$, round $L$ is reached with probability at least $1/2$.

At round $L$, the direct sample fails with probability at least $1/2$ for sufficiently small $a$. Conditional on its fresh amplification attempt, $j$ is uniform on $\{1,\ldots,M_L\}$, so [given, F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]
$
\mathbb E[j]=\frac1{M_L}\sum_{j=1}^{M_L}j=\frac{M_L+1}{2}\ge\frac{u}{2\sqrt a}.
$
The probability of reaching and entering this attempt is at least $1/4$, so this round alone contributes $\Omega(a^{-1/2})$ total access calls. For $a$ bounded away from zero, the first direct sample always makes one $A$-call while $a^{-1/2}$ is bounded, giving the same aggregate lower bound with a smaller constant.

If $a=0$, every round executes its direct preparation and the process never halts by [F2]. Finite-prefix expected query counts therefore grow without bound with the number of completed rounds, so their supremum in [F4] is $+\infty$. Gate and classical costs remain separate as required by [F5].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $|0\rangle\in H$ be a specified unit input vector, let $A:H\to H$ be a supplied measurement-free unitary, and let $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$. The access contract supplies and charges calls to $A$, its inverse $A^\dagger$, the good phase reflection
$
S_{\mathrm{good}}:=I_H-2\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},
$
and the zero-input phase reflection
$
S_0:=I_H-2|0\rangle\langle0|.
$
The signs are part of the contract: $S_{\mathrm{good}}$ is $-I$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ and $+I$ on its orthogonal complement. Reflection about the prepared state is the composite $A S_0 A^\dagger$, with its component calls charged unless a separate direct-reflection access is supplied.

Put $|\psi\rangle=A|0\rangle$ and define the initial success weight
$
a:=\|\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle\|^2\in[0,1].
$
When $a>0$, define $|G\rangle:=\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}|\psi\rangle/\sqrt a$. When $a<1$, define $|B\rangle:=(I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}})|\psi\rangle/\sqrt{1-a}$. These vectors are normalized and lie respectively in the range and kernel of $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$. If $a=0$ or $a=1$, the corresponding zero component is omitted and no vector is normalized from it. With this convention,
$
|\psi\rangle=\sqrt a\,|G\rangle+\sqrt{1-a}\,|B\rangle
$
means the sum of the nonzero component terms. Under the projective measurement $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I_H-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$, the probability of the good outcome is $a$; the finite-dimensional rank-one density and projective-measurement outcome laws are [[thm-qc-unit-vector-projector-is-density]] and [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

The output task may return the conditional quantum state after the good outcome; that state is defined only on a positive-probability branch and is supported in $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ by [[thm-qc-projective-conditional-state]]. A classical output additionally requires $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$ to be diagonal in a specified output basis and a costed coherent or ordinary verifier. An arbitrary projection does not supply a classical predicate.

Input a prepared sampler $A$, a success projection $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$, an integer $m\ge0$, and phases $\phi,\varphi\in[0,2\pi)$. In addition to $A,A^\dagger$, the access contract must supply the exact phase operations
$
S_0(\phi)=I+(e^{i\phi}-1)|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad
S_{\mathrm{good}}(\varphi)=I+(e^{i\varphi}-1)\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},
$
and charge each call. Such access does not follow from a $\pi$-phase reflection alone. Prepare $A|0\rangle$, apply
$
Q(\phi,\varphi):=-A S_0(\phi)A^\dagger S_{\mathrm{good}}(\varphi)
$
exactly $m$ times, and apply the declared good/bad projective instrument. Return the conditional quantum output on a positive-probability good branch or fail on the bad branch. A classical output additionally needs the diagonal-predicate and costed-verifier conditions in [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]].

In the ordered basis $(|G\rangle,|B\rangle)$, write $u=e^{i\phi}$ and $v=e^{i\varphi}$. Since $A|0\rangle=|\psi\rangle$, [given, F1, F2, algebra]
$
A S_0(\phi)A^\dagger=I+(u-1)|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|.
$
Multiplying on the right by $S_{\mathrm{good}}(\varphi)=\operatorname{diag}(v,1)$ and including the scalar minus gives
$
Q=-\begin{pmatrix}
v((1-a)+au)&(u-1)\sqrt{a(1-a)}\\
v(u-1)\sqrt{a(1-a)}&a+(1-a)u
\end{pmatrix}.
$
This calculation also shows directly that the good/bad plane is invariant.

Equality of the diagonal entries is equivalent to [given, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]
$
v=\frac{a+(1-a)u}{(1-a)+au}.
$
For $\phi\ne\pi$, $\cos(\phi/2)\ne0$, and after multiplying numerator and denominator by $e^{-i\phi/2}$, the quotient is
$
\frac{x+iy}{x-iy},\qquad x=\cos(\phi/2),\quad y=(1-2a)\sin(\phi/2).
$
By [F3], this equals $e^{i\varphi}$ exactly when $\tan(\varphi/2)=y/x=(1-2a)\tan(\phi/2)$; cross-multiplication of $(1+it)/(1-it)$ shows the equivalence in both directions. On $[0,2\pi)\setminus\{\pi\}$, the half-angle tangent takes each real value exactly once, so the branch is unique.

If $\phi=0$, the quotient in step 2.1 is $1$, hence $\varphi=0$. If $\phi=\pi$, the diagonal equality becomes $2a-1=-e^{i\varphi}(2a-1)$. For $a\ne1/2$, this is equivalent to $e^{i\varphi}=-1$, hence $\varphi=\pi$; for $a=1/2$, both diagonal entries are zero for every phase. At $a=0$ or $1$, one normalized component in [F1] is absent, so a two-dimensional diagonal comparison is not defined.
